thought.text: The Gradle daemon was killed — likely OOM (7.6 GB total RAM shared with the emulator). Let me confirm and tune:

reasoning_content:
The Gradle daemon was "forcibly terminated or crashed" — probably the OOM killer (7.6 GB RAM: emulator ~1.5–2GB + Gradle daemon heap 1.5GB + Kotlin daemon + NDK... could exceed it). Check dmesg / meminfo and the Gradle daemon logs.

Countermeasures:
1. Lower the daemon's memory in gradle.properties (org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx1536m, also consider -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize).
2. Consider stopping the emulator during the build (to free up RAM) and then restarting it afterward (does the emulator retain its state? Without snapshots it reboots, but that's fine).
3. Check whether the OOM killer really fired.

action.command: free -h; dmesg 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "killed process|oom" | tail -5; grep -n "maxHeapSize\|jvmargs" /workspace/android/gradle.properties /root/fvm/versions/3.35.7/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/*.gradle 2>/dev/null | head
